title: MacSync macOS Stealer Exploits ClickFix Lures to Steal Credentials and Cryptocurrency Wallets
content_md: MacSync, a macOS-focused information stealer and remote-access stager sold through a malware-as-a-service (MaaS) model, is targeting Apple users through ClickFix lures, search-engine malvertising, and fake software download pages. The malware relies on social engineering instead of exploiting a software vulnerability. Victims are directed to fraudulent pages impersonating popular brands, including Google Meet, Zoom, Claude AI , ChatGPT, Cloudflare, Docker, Notion, Cursor, TradingView, and cryptocurrency applications. The pages display fake errors, CAPTCHA checks, or installation prompts that instruct users to copy and run a command in macOS Terminal. Once executed, the command launches a lightweight native Mach-O stager. The malicious binary silently detaches from the Terminal session using the fork() and setsid() functions, then redirects standard input, output, and error streams to /dev/null . This prevents visible error messages and helps the malware operate in the background without alerting the victim. MacSync samples also use single-byte XOR obfuscation with the 0xAA key to hide command strings, temporary paths, API headers, and command-and-control (C2) addresses from static security scans. The sample analyzed was an ad-hoc signed 64-bit x86_64 Mach-O executable using the signing identifier com.utils.Launcher .
